prerequisites: Resistencia de Materiales I y II

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacities to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Knowledge and capacities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering whose objective is: the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacture, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in competence 61.
Collaborate proactively in the development of work, establishing goals and meeting objectives.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.
Extract conclusions from practical or experimental work and research carried out autonomously.

syllabus_topics: Wind girder, Saint Andrew's cross and perimeter beam
teaching_methods: Participative lecture, conferences, company visits, attendance at fairs, etc.
Individual or group resolution of cases, role-playing, application technique exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Realization of a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design and execution of a series of activities

Personalized and small group attention. Instruction carried out with the objective of reviewing, redirecting class materials, learning and carrying out assignments, etc. Specific student consultations. Scheduled tutorials.
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem solving, projects, etc. For submission and presentation in practical classes.
Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation, etc.

assessment_methods.method: Reports and results of practical execution tests

assessment_rules: For the 1st call, the final grade is the sum of written test scores (55% weight) and individual/group work (45% weight). A minimum total score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. For the 2nd call, students can choose to keep the practical work score (45% weight) and approved partial exams; in this case, a single exam will have a weight of 65%. Alternatively, if the project score is not kept, the exam will weigh 100%, which must be explicitly indicated before the exam. Use of AI is regulated in three levels; unauthorized use in Level 1 (e.g., in-person exams) or undeclared/uncited use in Level 2 (e.g., support for learning) or lacking full traceability in Level 3 (intensive use) is considered plagiarism and may result in a 0 for the instrument or even failing the course.
